facts.fact_text: The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 12 January 2013 in Baku.
The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 26 January 2013 in Baku.
Information about the demonstrations was disseminated through Facebook or the press.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
According to the applicant, the participants in the demonstration of 12 January 2013 were drawing the public's attention to the deaths of soldiers in the army.
According to the applicant, the participants in the demonstration of 26 January 2013 were condemning the use of force by the police against those who had participated in previous demonstrations.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
At the time of both of the applicant's arrests, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.
Shortly after the demonstration of 12 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
Following his arrest on 12 January 2013, the applicant was taken to a police station where he was questioned.
Following his arrest on 26 January 2013, the applicant was taken to a police station where he was questioned.
On the day of the applicant's arrest on 12 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.
On the day of the applicant's arrest on 26 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.

The administrative-offence report issued on 12 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).

The administrative-offence report issued on 26 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).
In the first case (arrest of 12 January 2013), after having been held for a few hours in police custody, the applicant was released.
In the first case (arrest of 12 January 2013), the applicant's release was subject to an undertaking to reappear at the police station on 14 January 2013.
In the first case (arrest of 12 January 2013), the applicant was brought before the Nasimi District Court on 14 January 2013, the day he reappeared at the police station.
In the second case (arrest of 26 January 2013), the applicant was brought before the Nasimi District Court on 26 January 2013, the day of his arrest.
In the first case, the Nasimi District Court found that the applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
In the second case, the Nasimi District Court found that the applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
By decision of 14 January 2013, the Nasimi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences in the first case.
By decision of 26 January 2013, the Nasimi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences in the second case.
In the first case, the Nasimi District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN).
In the second case, the Nasimi District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of AZN 400.
In the first case, on 25 January 2013, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court.
In the second case, on 6 February 2013, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court.
No prior notice was given to the Baku City Executive Authority by the organisers of the demonstration planned for 12 January 2013.
No prior notice was given to the Baku City Executive Authority by the organisers of the demonstration planned for 26 January 2013.
The Baku City Executive Authority was the relevant authority to receive prior notice of demonstrations.

On the day of the applicant's arrest on 26 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.

The administrative-offence report issued on 12 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).

The administrative-offence report issued on 26 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).
At the time of both of the applicant's arrests, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

Before the amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, which entered into force on 1 January 2013, any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 by a reprimand or a fine of AZN 7 to 13.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Both of the applicant's arrests occurred after the amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 were enacted.

At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets by an organiser of an assembly who is an individual shall be punished by a fine of AZN 1,500 to 3,000; or, depending on the circumstances of the case and the personality of the perpetrator of the offence, by community service for 200 to 240 hours or administrative detention for up to 15 days.
At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a person in charge shall be punished by a fine of AZN 3,000 to 6,000.
At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a legal entity shall be punished by a fine of AZN 15,000 to 30,000.

At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that participation in an assembly, a demonstration, a protest, a march or a picket which was not organised in accordance with the rules set forth under the legislation shall be punishable by a fine of AZN 300 to 600; or, depending on the circumstances of the case and the personality of the perpetrator of the offence, by community service for 160 to 200 hours or administrative detention for up to 15 days.

The Note to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that if there are elements of a crime in actions proscribed under Articles 298.1 and 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the perpetrator of those actions bears criminal responsibility under the relevant Articles of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

Other relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings, relevant provisions concerning the organisation and holding of public assemblies, and relevant extracts of international documents are summarised in the judgment in the case of Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, paragraphs 27-42, 15 October 2015).

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', stated that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the establishment of an inclusive political system and a truly competitive and unrestrictive political environment requires full implementation of basic freedoms, including freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and freedom of association.
Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about the situation regarding basic freedoms in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive use of certain articles of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan, in particular Articles 221 and 233, against participants in peaceful, albeit unauthorised, demonstrations.
Report CommDH(2013)14 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, was issued on 6 August 2013 following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner is deeply concerned by the recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner is of the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner urges the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
